reader_question: How close did the Senate come to the 60 votes it needs to end debate on taking up H.R. 7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act?
grade_line: Documented: the Senate’s record of roll call vote 253
title: The Senate fell seven votes short of the 60 needed to take up the House’s bill to limit members’ stock purchases and require photo ID to vote in federal elections.
measure_line: Senate roll call vote 253, September 30, 2026, on cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act, the vote to end debate on taking the bill up: yes and no votes of the 100 senators, by party as the Senate records it
notes: Cloture on a motion to proceed ends debate on whether to take a bill up, and it needs three-fifths of the Senate, 60 votes.
The House passed H.R. 7008 by 232 to 198 on July 22, 2026, in roll call 280: Republicans 218 to 0, Democrats 13 to 198 with one not voting, and the one independent yes.
alt: A bar of the Senate’s 100 votes, its 53 yes votes solid and its 47 no votes in outline, with a tick at the 60 needed to end debate and a bracket marking the seven-vote gap. All 53 yes votes were Republican; 45 Democrats and 2 independents voted no.

table.caption: Senate roll call vote 253 on H.R. 7008, September 30, 2026, by party

chart_notes: The bar runs to 100 senators: the 53 yes votes fill it solid and the 47 no votes in outline, in one ink. A tick marks the 60 votes needed, and a bracket under the bar the seven votes the yes side lacked.
